Appendix A
Lifting to Chain Level

We will now define (partial) chain lifts of various bimodule morphisms in
\textnormal{BSBim}(\mathfrak{h},W)
. Specifically, given a morphism
f
between Bott-Samelson bimodules, we will define a (partial) morphism between the corresponding Bott-Samelson complexes lifting
f
. As our maps are required to be
R^{e}
linear it suffices to define the chain maps on the inner tensor factors of
R^{e},R^{ee},
etc. In addition, as all of the bimodule maps we are lifting are of the form
f:R\otimes_{s/t}\ldots\otimes_{s/t}R\to R\otimes_{s/t}\ldots\otimes_{s/t}R
, we can always define
\widetilde{f}^{0}:R\otimes\ldots\otimes R\to R\otimes\ldots\otimes R
by the exact same formula as
f
but with
\otimes_{s/t}
replaced by
\otimes
.

A.1 Unit

The unit map of
B_{s}
will be
\eta_{s}:R\to B_{s}
where
\eta_{s}(1)=\rho_{s}\otimes_{s}1-1\otimes_{s}s(\rho_{s})
. We want to find
\widetilde{\eta_{s}}^{1}
making the following diagram commute.

{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\cdots}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\underline{V^{*}}(-2)\boxtimes R^{e}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\underline{1}\boxtimes R^{e}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces R}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\cdots}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces(\underline{(V^{*})^{s}}(-2)\oplus\mathbbm{k}\underline{\rho_{s}s(\rho_{s})}(-4))\boxtimes R^{e}(1)}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\underline{1}\boxtimes R^{e}(1)}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces B_{s}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces d}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\widetilde{\eta_{s}}^{1}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\widetilde{\eta_{s}}^{0}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\Delta}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces d}

Recall that
V^{*}=(V^{*})^{s}\oplus\mathbbm{k}\rho_{s}
. We then claim that the following definition will make the diagram commute

\displaystyle\widetilde{\eta_{s}}^{1}(\underline{r}\boxtimes 1\otimes 1)

\displaystyle=\underline{r}\boxtimes\rho_{s}\otimes 1-\underline{r}\boxtimes 1\otimes s(\rho_{s})\quad\textnormal{ if }r\in(V^{*})^{s}

\displaystyle\widetilde{\eta_{s}}^{1}(\underline{\rho_{s}}\boxtimes 1\otimes 1)

\displaystyle=(\underline{\rho_{s}+s(\rho_{s})})\boxtimes\rho_{s}\otimes 1-\underline{\rho_{s}s(\rho_{s})}\boxtimes 1\otimes 1

This is clear if
r\in(V^{*})^{s}
. For
\rho_{s}
note that
\widetilde{\eta_{s}}^{0}(d(\underline{\rho_{s}}\boxtimes 1\otimes 1))
is given by
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\underline{\rho_{s}}\boxtimes 1\otimes 1}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\underline{1}\boxtimes\left(\rho_{s}\otimes 1-1\otimes\rho_{s}\right)}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces?}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\underline{1}\boxtimes\left(\rho_{s}\rho_{s}\otimes 1-\rho_{s}\otimes s(\rho_{s})-\rho_{s}\otimes\rho_{s}+1\otimes\rho_{s}s(\rho_{s})\right)}

and one quickly computes that
d
applied to our definition above yields the expression on the bottom right.

A.2 Multiplication

The multiplication map of
B_{s}
is
\mu_{s}:R\otimes_{s}R\otimes_{s}R(2)\to R\otimes_{s}R(1)
where
\mu_{s}(f\otimes_{s}g\otimes_{s}h)=\partial_{s}(g)f\otimes_{s}h
. We want to find
\widetilde{\mu_{s}}^{1}
making this diagram commute. Let
W=((V^{*})^{s}(-2)\oplus\mathbbm{k}\rho_{s}s(\rho_{s})(-4))
.

{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\cdots}

{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\underline{1}\boxtimes R^{ee}(2)}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces B_{s}\otimes_{R}B_{s}}

\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\widetilde{\mu_{s}}^{0}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\mu_{s}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces d}

We claim that the following definition will work.

\displaystyle\widetilde{\mu_{s}}^{1}(\underline{r^{(1)}}\boxtimes 1\otimes h\otimes 1)

\displaystyle=0\quad\textnormal{ if }r\in(V^{*})^{s}

\displaystyle\widetilde{\mu_{s}}^{1}(\underline{\rho_{s}s(\rho_{s})^{(1)}}\boxtimes 1\otimes h\otimes 1)

\displaystyle=0

\displaystyle\widetilde{\mu_{s}}^{1}(\underline{r^{(2)}}\boxtimes 1\otimes h\otimes 1)

\displaystyle=\underline{r}\boxtimes\partial_{s}(h)\otimes 1\quad\textnormal{ if }r\in(V^{*})^{s}

\displaystyle=\underline{\rho_{s}s(\rho_{s})}\boxtimes\partial_{s}(h)\otimes 1

Appendix B
HOMFLY Homology Calculations

We refer the reader to
[
EMTW20
, Chapter 21.6]
for the definition of HOMFLY homology
\mathrm{HHH}
. As shown in
[
Kho07
, Theorem 1]
, the reduced HOMFLY homology
\overline{\mathrm{HHH}}
is computed using the geometric realization
\mathfrak{h}_{geo}
of
S_{n}
. As a result, the complex
F(\beta_{L})
associated to a braid
\beta_{L}
lives in
K^{b}(\mathbb{S}\textnormal{Bim}(\mathfrak{h}_{geo},S_{n}))
and
R
is a polynomial ring in
n-1
variables instead of
n
. In this section we will be computing reduced HOMFLY homology. The reduced HOMFLY homology categorifies the reduced HOMFLY polynomial
\overline{P(a,q)}
defined via the skein relation

a^{-1}\overline{P(a,q)}(L_{+})-a\overline{P(a,q)}(L_{-})=(q-q^{-1})\overline{P(a,q)}(L_{0})

and the normalization
\overline{P(a,q)}(\mathrm{unknot})=1
.

Definition B.1
.

Define
d_{s}=\frac{1}{2}(\alpha_{s}\otimes_{s}1-1\otimes_{s}\alpha_{s})\in R\otimes_{R^{s}}R
.

As a result, one can calculate that
\overline{\mathrm{HHH}}^{A=0}(F(\sigma_{1}^{2})),\overline{\mathrm{HHH}}^{A=1}(F(\sigma_{1}^{2}))
will be the cohomology of the following complexes

\overline{\mathrm{HHH}}^{A=0}(F(\sigma_{1}^{2})):\boxed{R(-2)}\xrightarrow{0}R\xrightarrow{\alpha_{s}}R(2)\qquad\overline{\mathrm{HHH}}^{A=1}(F(\sigma_{1}^{2})):\boxed{R(2)}\xrightarrow{0}R(4)\xrightarrow{\mathrm{id}}R(4)

where
R=\mathbbm{k}[\alpha_{s}]
as
(\sigma_{1})^{2}
is a braid on 2 strands. The Poincare series
\overline{\mathscr{P}(A,Q,T)}(F(\sigma_{1}^{2}))
for
\overline{\mathrm{HHH}}(F(\sigma_{1}^{2}))
will be

\overline{\mathscr{P}(A,Q,T)}(F(\sigma_{1}^{2}))=\left(\frac{Q^{2}}{1-Q^{2}}+Q^{-2}T^{2}\right)+A\left(\frac{Q^{-2}}{1-Q^{2}}\right)

To recover the HOMFLY polynomial
P(a,q)
up to a unit in
\mathbb{Z}\llbracket A^{\pm 1},Q^{\pm 1},T^{\pm 1}\rrbracket
we make the following substitutions

A=-a^{2}q^{2},T=-1,Q=q

(B.1)

Applying this to
\overline{\mathscr{P}(A,Q,T)}(F(\sigma_{1}^{2}))
we obtain

\overline{\mathscr{P}(A,Q,T)}(F(\sigma_{1}^{2}))|_{\lx@cref{creftype\lx@tilde refnum}{subeq}}=\frac{q^{2}+q^{-2}-1-a^{2}}{1-q^{2}}=\frac{q^{2}+q^{-2}-1-a^{2}}{-q(q-q^{-1})}

while using the definition of the reduced HOMFLY polynomial above we obtain

\overline{P(a,q)}(\widehat{\sigma_{1}^{2}})=a\left(\frac{q^{2}+q^{-2}-1-a^{2}}{q-q^{-1}}\right)

which after multiplying by the unit
-(aq)^{-1}
agrees with
\overline{\mathscr{P}(A,Q,T)}(F(\sigma_{1}^{2}))|_{\lx@cref{creftype\lx@tilde refnum}{subeq}}
.

\overline{\mathscr{P}(A,Q,T)}(F(\sigma_{1}^{2}))^{2}

\overline{\mathrm{HHH}}(\beta_{1}\#\beta_{2})=\overline{\mathrm{HHH}}(\beta_{1})\otimes_{\mathbbm{k}}\overline{\mathrm{HHH}}(\beta_{2})

T=-1

T=-1
will then be

\frac{2Q^{-4}}{(1-Q^{2})^{2}}-\frac{Q^{-2}}{(1-Q^{2})^{2}}-\frac{1}{(1-Q^{2})^{2}}=\frac{Q^{-4}(2+Q^{2})}{1-Q^{2}}

\overline{\mathrm{HHH}}(T(3,-3))^{A=2}
after accounting for the
Q^{-4}
shift from
Lemma

B.6
is

A^{2}\left(T^{-4}Q^{-2}+T^{-2}Q^{-6}+\frac{T^{-1}Q^{-8}(2+Q^{2})}{1-Q^{2}}+\frac{Q^{-10}}{(1-Q^{2})^{2}}\right)

The total Poincare series for
\overline{\mathrm{HHH}}(T(3,-3))^{A=0}
after accounting for the
Q^{-4}
shift from
Lemma

B.6
is
\frac{1}{(1-Q^{2})^{2}}
. Putting this all together, we obtain

\displaystyle\overline{\mathscr{P}(A,Q,T)}(F((\sigma_{1}^{-1}\sigma_{2}^{-1})^{3}))=\frac{1}{(1-Q^{2})^{2}}+A\left(T^{-2}Q^{-2}+\frac{T^{-1}Q^{-4}(2+Q^{2})}{1-Q^{2}}+\frac{Q^{-6}+Q^{-4}}{(1-Q^{2})^{2}}\right)

\displaystyle+A^{2}\left(T^{-4}Q^{-2}+T^{-2}Q^{-6}+\frac{T^{-1}Q^{-8}(2+Q^{2})}{1-Q^{2}}+\frac{Q^{-10}}{(1-Q^{2})^{2}}\right)

(B.5)

The HOMFLY polynomial for
L6n1\left\{0,1\right\}
, the braid closure of
(\sigma_{1}^{-1}\sigma_{2}^{-1})^{3}
is computed in
[
LM25
]
and is

\overline{P(a,q)}(L6n1\left\{0,1\right\})=-\frac{3}{v^{6}}+\frac{3}{v^{4}}+\frac{1}{v^{8}z^{2}}-\frac{2}{v^{6}z^{2}}+\frac{1}{v^{4}z^{2}}-\frac{z^{2}}{v^{6}}+\frac{4z^{2}}{v^{4}}+\frac{z^{4}}{v^{4}}

where
z=q-q^{-1}
and
v=a
. After mutliplying by the unit
a^{8}/q^{2}
, this agrees with
\overline{\mathscr{P}(A,Q,T)}(F((\sigma_{1}^{-1}\sigma_{2}^{-1})^{3}))|_{\lx@cref{creftype\lx@tilde refnum}{subeq}}
.

Appendix C
Gomi’s Trace

Before going into Gomi’s trace, we should mention that there are usually two versions/presentations of the Hecke algebra
\mathbf{H}_{W}
of a Coxeter group
W
in the literature. As originally defined in
[
KL79
]
, version 1 of
\mathbf{H}_{W}
is the associative algebra over
\mathbb{Z}[q,q^{-1}]
on generators
\left\{T_{s}\right\}
satisfying the braid relation and the quadratic relation

T_{s}^{2}=(q-1)T_{s}+q

In
[
Soe97
]
, Soergel gives the second presentation of
\mathbf{H}_{W}
as the associative algebra over
\mathbb{Z}[v,v^{-1}]
on generators
\left\{\delta_{s}\right\}
satisfying the braid relation and the quadratic relation

\delta_{s}^{2}=(v^{-1}-v)\delta_{s}+1

and the two presentations are isomorphic under the
\mathbb{Z}-
linear map
\delta_{w}\mapsto v^{\ell(w)}T_{w}
and
v\mapsto q^{-1/2}
after tensoring version 1 by
\otimes_{\mathbb{Z}}\mathbb{Z}[q^{1/2},q^{-1/2}]
. Under this isomorphism we also have
\delta_{s}^{-1}=v^{-1}T_{s}^{-1}
. For
w\in W=W_{m}
, the KL-basis of
H_{W_{m}}
can be explicitly expressed in the standard basis as

b_{w}=\sum_{y\leq w}v^{\ell(w)-\ell(y)}\delta_{y}=v^{\ell(w)}\sum_{y\leq w}T_{y}

(C.1)

[
Gom06
]
uses version 1 of
\mathbf{H}_{W}
while
[
EMTW20
]
uses version 2 and as such we will be using both presentations interchangeably in what follows. Let
\mathrm{HH}^{a,b}(M)=\mathrm{Ext}_{R^{e}}^{a,b}(R,M)
and
B_{w}\in\mathbb{S}\textnormal{Bim}(\mathfrak{h}_{geo},W_{m})
.

Definition C.1
.

Define a trace
\epsilon_{t}:\mathbf{H}_{W_{m}}\to\mathbb{Z}[q^{1/2},q^{-1/2}][t]
by first defining
\epsilon_{t}
on the KL-basis via

\epsilon_{t}(b_{w})=(1-q^{-1})^{2}\sum_{a,b}\dim_{\mathbbm{k}}\mathrm{HH}^{a,b}(B_{w})q^{-b/2}t^{a}=\mathrm{grk}_{R}^{t}(\mathrm{HH}^{\bullet,\bullet}({B_{w}}))

and extend
\mathbb{Z}[q^{1/2},q^{-1/2}]
linearly where
\mathrm{grk}_{R}^{t}(M)=av^{k}t^{n}
if
M\cong R(-k)^{\oplus a}[-n]
.

Remark
.

In order for
\epsilon_{t}
to be
\mathbb{Z}[q^{1/2},q^{-1/2}]
linear, at the categorical level we should define
q^{1/2}[B_{w}]:=[B_{w}(1)]
. Consequently this means that we should define
v^{-1}[B_{w}]:=[B_{w}(1)]
which is the opposite of what is written in
[
EMTW20
, Section 4.8]
. In fact, Soergel’s Hom formula
[
EMTW20
, Theorem 5.27]
is only true when using our convention above, rather than the convention in
[
EMTW20
]
.

As we are in the geometric realization,
Theorem

7.12
tells us that for
1\leq k\leq m

\epsilon_{t}(b_{{}_{t}\widehat{k}})=\epsilon_{t}(b_{{}_{s}\widehat{k}})=q^{-k/2}+(q^{(4-k)/2}+q^{k/2})t+q^{(k+4)/2}t^{2}

(C.2)

Lemma C.2
.

(a)

For all
2\leq k\leq m-1

(v+v^{-1})\epsilon_{t}(b_{{}_{s}\widehat{k}})=\epsilon_{t}(b_{{}_{s}\widehat{k+1}})+\epsilon_{t}(b_{{}_{s}\widehat{k-1}})

(C.3)

(b)

\epsilon_{t}(\delta_{{}_{t}\widehat{k}})=\epsilon_{t}(\delta_{{}_{s}\widehat{k}})
.

(c)

\epsilon_{t}(\delta_{{}_{s}\widehat{k+1}})=(v^{-1}-v)\epsilon_{t}(\delta_{{}_{s}\widehat{k}})+\epsilon_{t}(\delta_{{}_{s}\widehat{k-1}})
for all
2\leq k\leq m-1
.

Proof.

(a)
follows from direct computation using
Eq.

C.2
.
(b)
follows from
Eq.

C.2
and induction using
Eq.

C.1
.

(c)
Using
Eq.

C.1
to expand the LHS of
Eq.

C.3
we obtain
v\epsilon_{t}(b_{{}_{s}\widehat{k}})+v^{-1}\epsilon_{t}(\delta_{{}_{s}\widehat{k}})+\epsilon_{t}(\delta_{{}_{t}\widehat{k-1}})+\epsilon_{t}(b_{{}_{s}\widehat{k-1}})
while the RHS of
Eq.

C.3
can be written as
\epsilon_{t}(\delta_{{}_{s}\widehat{k+1}})+v\epsilon_{t}(\delta_{{}_{t}\widehat{k}})+v\epsilon_{t}(b_{{}_{s}\widehat{k}})+\epsilon_{t}(b_{{}_{s}\widehat{k-1}})
. Thus it follows that

v^{-1}\epsilon_{t}(\delta_{{}_{s}\widehat{k}})+\epsilon_{t}(\delta_{{}_{t}\widehat{k-1}})=\epsilon_{t}(\delta_{{}_{s}\widehat{k+1}})+v\epsilon_{t}(\delta_{{}_{t}\widehat{k}})

and using part
(b)
and moving
v\epsilon_{t}(\delta_{{}_{t}\widehat{k}})
to the LHS gives the result.
∎

Let
\tau_{W_{m}}
be Gomi’s trace for
\mathbf{H}_{W_{m}}
as defined in
[
Gom06
, Section 4.2]
. For
W_{m}
, it turns out we do not need to know the entries of Lusztig’s Exotic Fourier transform matrix (although they are explicitly given in
[
Gom06
, Section 4.6]
) or even the characters of
\mathbf{H}_{W_{m}}
in order to compute
\tau_{W_{m}}
by the following result
[
Gom06
, Theorem 4.5]

Theorem C.3
.

Let
\displaystyle z=\frac{(q-1)r}{1+r}
. Then
\tau_{W_{m}}:\mathbf{H}_{W_{m}}\to\mathbb{Z}[q^{1/2},q^{-1/2}][z]
is the unique trace
10
10

10

This means that
\tau_{W_{m}}
is a
\mathbb{Z}[q^{1/2},q^{-1/2}]
linear map such that
\tau_{W_{m}}(ab)=\tau_{W_{m}}(ba)
for all
a,b\in\mathbf{H}_{W_{m}}
function on
\mathbf{H}_{W_{m}}
satisfying

(1)

\tau_{W_{m}}(1)=1

(2)

\displaystyle\tau_{W_{m}}(T_{1})=\tau_{W_{m}}(T_{2})=z

(3)

\tau_{W_{m}}(\underbrace{T_{1}T_{2}\ldots}_{i+1}\underbrace{\ldots T_{1}^{-1}T_{2}^{-1}}_{i-1})=z^{2}
, for all
\displaystyle 1\leq i\leq\left\lfloor\frac{m-1}{2}\right\rfloor

Theorem C.4
.

For all
x\in\mathbf{H}_{W_{m}}

\frac{1}{(1+qt)^{2}}\epsilon_{t}(x)=\tau_{W_{m}}(x)|_{r=qt}

Proof.

Because we have an isomorphism of doubly graded
vector spaces

\mathrm{HH}^{a,b}(M\otimes_{R}N)\cong\mathrm{HH}^{a,b}(N\otimes_{R}M)

the LHS is a trace function on
\mathbf{H}_{W_{m}}
and by uniqueness we just need to check the LHS satisfies the conditions in
Theorem

C.3
.
(1)
follows from the well known computation
\mathrm{HH}_{\bullet,\bullet}(R)=\mathrm{Sym}(V^{*}(-2))\otimes_{\mathbbm{k}}\Lambda^{\bullet}(V\llbracket-1\rrbracket)
, where
\dim V=2
in this case.
(2)
is an immediate consequence of
Eq.

C.2
and that
T_{s}=q^{1/2}b_{s}-1
.

For
(3)
, under the isomorphism between the two versions of the hecke algebra we have that

\epsilon_{t}(\underbrace{T_{1}T_{2}\ldots}_{i+1}\underbrace{\ldots T_{1}^{-1}T_{2}^{-1}}_{i-1})=v^{-2}\epsilon_{t}(\underbrace{\delta_{1}\delta_{2}\ldots}_{i+1}\underbrace{\ldots\delta_{1}^{-1}\delta_{2}^{-1}}_{i-1})

For
i\geq 1
, let
\varphi_{i}=\underbrace{\delta_{1}\delta_{2}\ldots}_{i+1}\underbrace{\ldots\delta_{1}^{-1}\delta_{2}^{-1}}_{i-1}
and
\varphi_{i}^{*}=\underbrace{\delta_{2}\delta_{1}\ldots}_{i+1}\underbrace{\ldots\delta_{2}^{-1}\delta_{1}^{-1}}_{i-1}
. We claim

\epsilon_{t}(\varphi_{i})=\epsilon_{t}(\varphi_{i-1}^{*})

and therefore we only need to compute
\epsilon_{t}(\varphi_{1})=\epsilon_{t}(\varphi_{1}^{*})
. Note
\delta_{2}^{-1}=\delta_{2}+v-v^{-1}
and since
\epsilon_{t}
is a trace we see that

\epsilon_{t}(\varphi_{i})=\epsilon_{t}((\delta_{2}+v-v^{-1})\delta_{1}\varphi_{i-1}^{*})=\epsilon_{t}(\delta_{2}\delta_{1}\varphi_{i-1}^{*})+(v-v^{-1})\epsilon_{t}(\delta_{1}\varphi_{i-1}^{*})

Now, using the quadratic relation, because
\varphi_{i}
alternates between
\delta_{1},\delta_{2}
at the start,
\delta_{1}^{-1},\delta_{2}^{-1}
at the end with 2 more
\delta_{1},\delta_{2}
terms than
\delta_{1}^{-1},\delta_{2}^{-1}
terms, we can write
\displaystyle\varphi_{i-1}^{*}=\sum_{j=2}^{2i-2}a_{j}\delta_{{}_{2}\widehat{j}}
when
i>1
. Because
\delta_{2}\delta_{1}\delta_{{}_{2}\widehat{j}}=\delta_{{}_{2}\widehat{j+2}}
, by
Lemma

C.2
part
(c)
we have

\displaystyle\epsilon_{t}(\delta_{2}\delta_{1}\varphi_{i-1}^{*})+(v-v^{-1})\epsilon_{t}(\delta_{1}\varphi_{i-1}^{*})

\displaystyle=(v^{-1}-v)\epsilon_{t}(\delta_{1}\varphi_{i-1}^{*})+\epsilon_{t}(\varphi_{i-1}^{*})+(v-v^{-1})\epsilon_{t}(\delta_{1}\varphi_{i-1}^{*})

\displaystyle=\epsilon_{t}(\varphi_{i-1}^{*})

as desired. Finally, using the above and
Eq.

C.2
we compute

\displaystyle\frac{1}{(1+qt)^{2}}\epsilon_{t}(\underbrace{T_{1}T_{2}\ldots}_{i+1}\underbrace{\ldots T_{1}^{-1}T_{2}^{-1}}_{i-1})

\displaystyle=\frac{1}{(1+qt)^{2}}v^{-2}\epsilon_{t}(\delta_{1}\delta_{2})=\frac{1}{(1+qt)^{2}}\epsilon_{t}(T_{1}T_{2})

\displaystyle=\frac{1}{(1+qt)^{2}}\left[q\epsilon_{t}(b_{12})-\epsilon_{t}(T_{1})-\epsilon_{t}(T_{2})-\epsilon_{t}(1)\right]

\displaystyle=\frac{(1+q^{2}t)^{2}-2(1+qt)(q-1)qt-(1+qt)^{2}}{(1+qt)^{2}}

\displaystyle=\left(\frac{(1-q)qt}{1+qt}\right)^{2}

∎

Corollary C.5
.

Let
\omega:\mathbf{H}_{W_{m}}\to\mathbf{H}_{W_{m}}
be the KL anti-involution. Given
B,B^{\prime}\in\mathbb{S}\textnormal{Bim}(\mathfrak{h}_{geo},W_{m})
set
v^{-1}[B]:=[B(1)]
.

\mathrm{grk}_{R}^{t}\mathrm{Ext}_{R^{e}}^{\bullet,\bullet}(B,B^{\prime})=(1+v^{-2}t)^{2}\tau_{W_{m}}\left(\omega(\mathrm{ch}_{\Delta}(B))\mathrm{ch}_{\Delta}(B^{\prime})\right)|_{r=v^{-2}t}

where
\mathrm{grk}_{R}^{t}(M)=cv^{k}t^{n}
if
M\cong R(-k)^{\oplus c}[-n]
.

Proof.

By adjunction,
Corollary

3.5
, and linearity it suffices to show this when
B=R,B^{\prime}=B_{w}
, but
\mathrm{ch}_{\Delta}(B_{w})=b_{w}
.
∎

By
[
Gom06
, Remark 4.2]
, when
z\to 0
(equivalently when
t\to 0
),
\tau_{W_{m}}\to\epsilon
where
\epsilon
is the standard/canonical trace on
\mathbf{H}_{W_{m}}
and thus the above corollary is a
t-
analog of Soergel’s Hom Formula
[
EMTW20
, Theorem 5.27]
.
